summary: Guidance requested: coordinated cron worker 'slotting' to avoid synchronized 429 storms on dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses during scheduled bulk uploads that run every 5 minutes across 40 workers after a recent API key rotation. Impact: Repeated token throttles causing ~30% of scheduled jobs to fail and backlog spikes in the customer's orchestrator. This is a business-critical nightly/real-time hybrid ingest; they are on a Dedicated pool and need guidance to avoid synchronized bursts.

Environment: prod, dedicated pool (us-east), tenant ID: df-9981 (provided in support thread). Workers use short-lived ephemeral API keys rotated every 24h; cron schedule: 40 parallel workers, each triggered every 5 minutes with <1s startup jitter.

Observed behavior: Starting ~2026-03-09 after key rotation, jobs report 429s within first 30s of start, subsequent retries hit throttling windows for up to 2 minutes. Console shows tenant token-window exhaustion with sawtooth refill spikes aligned to job start time.

Expected behavior: Smooth refill and ability to absorb the scheduled warmup without persistent 429s; or clear guidance on how to configure client-side staggering / server-side burst pools for this workload.

Attachments: sanitized request traces, timestamps, and token-window heatmap exported from console (attached in ticket metadata).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure 40 worker processes in a single tenant using ephemeral keys rotated daily.
2) Schedule each worker to run a bulk upload job every 5 minutes with <1s startup jitter.
3) Observe that immediately after a new rotation or after a scheduled tick, many workers begin at near-same time and receive 429s within 10-30s.
4) Retry behavior: client retries with default backoff produce high contention and the tenant token-window remains exhausted for ~90-120s.
logs: 2026-03-09T03:05:17Z influx: rate-limiter refill-attempt ts=161545 token_delta=0 window_ms=60000
console-heatmap: 03:05:00-03:07:00 tenant df-9981 token-usage spike aligned with scheduled job start
customer_notes: Customer confirms the only change was enforcing daily key rotation and increasing worker count from 20->40 2 weeks ago.
They attempted to add client-side random jitter of up to 1s but see no benefit.
Customer asks whether Redwood can recommend server-side configuration (burst pools, smoothing) and any client best-practices for cron-based workers.

2026-03-10 10:01 - Customer (J. Miller, DataFleet): Uploaded heatmap and three sample request IDs (sanitized). Confirmed short-lived keys and daily rotation. We tried jitter=1s, no change.

2026-03-10 11:48 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Initial hypothesis: synchronized job start + key rotation aligns refill windows and exhausts tenant-level token window. Asking for rate-limiter histograms and per-route accounting for the 03:05 spike.
2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Collected refill histogram. Observed ~95% of bursts fall inside first 10s of cron tick and refill smoothing not sufficient for this scale.

2026-03-11 08:20 - Support (Aisha Patel): Proposed immediate mitigations: increase client jitter to 30-60s, optionally pin a small set of long-lived service keys for staggered warmup, and request us to enable a temporary dedicated burst pool for tenant while long-term fix is planned.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Daily key rotation caused many workers to acquire new tokens at similar time -> ephemeral-key fanout increases concurrency accounting.
Hypothesis B: Client-side jitter was too small (<1s) to spread across refill window; token-window size and refill cadence produce sawtooth when many concurrent short-lived sessions start together.

Metrics observed: tenant token-window at peak hit 100% utilization for 90-120s; refill events are bucketed at 60s granularity; per-route accounting shows heavy weight on /v1/generate with model text-generation-v2.
Triage steps executed: reviewed token refill histograms, confirmed no ingress-side duplicate counting, validated ephemeral-key issuance logs, verified dedicated-pool autoscaler healthy.
Temporary mitigation tested: enabled per-tenant temporary burst pool and increased refill smoothing on-internal side -> immediate drop in 429s for next scheduled ticks.
Long-term risk: If client continues synchronized scheduling, persistent high-margin bursts will increase unit cost for tenant and could impact other tenants on shared fallback capacity.
resolution: Workaround and recommendations provided to customer: 1) Increase client-side jitter to 30-60s and add exponential backoff on retries; 2) Optionally allocate a small set (2-4) of long-lived service keys to rotate independently from short-lived keys so warmups are spread; 3) We enabled a temporary per-tenant burst pool for 48 hours to relieve immediate pressure; 4) Recommended server settings: enable per-route burst isolation for heavy /v1/generate routes and increase refill smoothing window to 90s for scheduled-worker tenants. 5) Follow-up: engineering to evaluate a 'slotting' feature (server-side scheduled-worker coordinator) to automatically stagger refill credits for cron-like patterns (created ENGINE-987). Customer accepted immediate mitigations and will test jitter=60s and long-lived key set. If mitigations fail, we'll coordinate dedicated autoscaler and permanent burst pool allocation.
